title: Adaptive Weight Sharing for Efficient NAS
statement: Weight sharing with adaptive allocation based on architecture similarity will improve NAS efficiency while maintaining accuracy compared to uniform weight sharing.
rationale: Evidence shows weight sharing reduces cost by 1000x but may sacrifice accuracy. Adaptive allocation could bridge this gap.
approach_summary: Implement a similarity-based weight allocation strategy in the supernet, measure accuracy vs uniform sharing on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.

title: Sparse Attention with Learned Patterns
statement: Learning sparse attention patterns end-to-end rather than using fixed patterns will achieve better accuracy-efficiency tradeoff in transformer architectures.
rationale: Current sparse attention uses fixed patterns. Learning them jointly with model parameters should improve results.
approach_summary: Train sparse attention pattern predictor alongside the main model, compare against fixed patterns on language modeling benchmarks.

title: Progressive Architecture Growing
statement: Starting with a small architecture and progressively growing it during training will find better architectures than searching in a fixed-size space.
rationale: Inspired by progressive training in GANs, growing architectures may explore the space more efficiently.
approach_summary: Implement progressive architecture growth with automated decision points for when to expand. Compare against fixed-size NAS.
